answer: Sybil resistance in AI agent economies can leverage a social graph of trust. Each AI agent is a vertex, its legitimacy strengthened by endorsements from other trusted agents. This provides a strong signal of authenticity. Attacking agents face high costs: they must compromise numerous existing vertices to generate credible endorsements for their fake identities. A compromised vertex might whisper warnings about suspicious activity. The collective cost of acquiring sufficient trust from the network's legitimate vertices makes large-scale Sybil attacks economically impractical.
